# Angular responsibility boundaries and the path to an updated screen

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `frontend-angular-architecture` · **Angular, TypeScript & Frontend Architecture** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S06-Q001](#S06-Q001)

<p>How is an Angular application organized, and how do its main parts collaborate when a user changes something on a page?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Explain and defend Angular boundaries by tracing one feature from navigation and input to state changes and a usable view.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace components, dependency injection and routing for a concrete user interaction.</li>
<li>Choose form and state ownership based on lifetime and collaboration needs.</li>
<li>Distinguish incorrect view updates from expensive rendering or code loading.</li>
<li>Define evidence for a loading or rendering change, including regressions.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [TypeScript guarantees and JavaScript behavior at browser boundaries](frontend-typescript-semantics.md)

<p>First establish the parts of the application and how dependencies connect them. Follow navigation into a feature, then explain the form and state that drive its view. This makes rendering failures diagnosable and gives state-management choices a concrete context; code splitting can then be judged by the loading experience it actually changes.</p>

### S06-Q001 · Foundation

<p>How is an Angular application organized, and how do its main parts collaborate when a user changes something on a page?</p>

**[S06-Q001](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q001)**

> Explain the core architecture of an Angular application.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the architecture through one concrete interaction. Architecture here means responsibilities and connections, rather than a list of Angular features.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace responsibility boundaries from a UI interaction to the resulting application state.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the Angular version and application setup; verify version-dependent architecture APIs in official documentation. Do not assume that every existing application uses the same bootstrapping style.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects components, services and application boundaries in a causal flow.</li>
<li>Explains which boundary would change when the feature grows and how to check that change.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Names framework features without showing how one interaction travels between them.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which responsibility would you move if two screens needed the same business operation?</li>
<li>How would you test that boundary without rendering the whole application?</li>

### S06-Q002 · Mechanism

<p>How does Angular resolve a component&#x27;s dependencies, and what determines whether two components receive the same service instance?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q002](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q002)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q002](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q002)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How does Angular Dependency Injection work?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Dependency injection supplies an object&#x27;s collaborators. Explain how the application resolves a requested dependency and how its registration affects the lifetime you rely on.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about dependency resolution and instance ownership across component boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the Angular version and provider locations in your example; check official documentation for the applicable injector model and APIs.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Uses a concrete component tree and provider configuration to justify instance sharing.</li>
<li>Identifies a state-isolation or testing consequence and an observable way to verify it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calls every service a singleton without examining its registration or injector boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you investigate state unexpectedly shared between two editor components?</li>
<li>What changes if a test supplies a different implementation of the dependency?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q003"></a>

### S06-Q003 · Mechanism

<p>What happens when a user navigates to an Angular route that loads code lazily, and how would you choose that loading boundary?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q003](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q003)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q003](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q003)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain routing and lazy loading.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Lazy loading defers loading a portion of application code until it is needed. Describe navigation and loading as one user-visible flow, including an unsuccessful load.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain route-to-screen execution and justify a loading boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the Angular version, route configuration and navigation scenario; confirm the relevant router APIs in official documentation. Distinguish first navigation from revisiting the route.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces navigation, loading and screen availability without assuming code is already present.</li>
<li>Supports the chosen boundary with observable loading behavior and a failure-handling plan.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treats lazy loading as an automatic performance improvement without considering the navigation delay.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should the user see if the route&#x27;s code cannot be downloaded?</li>
<li>What evidence would make you preload this route instead?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S06-Q008 · Application

<p>How would you model and validate a nontrivial Angular reactive form, including errors returned by the server?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q008](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q008)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q008](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q008)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain reactive forms and validation.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A reactive form represents input and validation state explicitly. Describe the path from editing a field to deciding whether submission can succeed.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Connect form state, validation and submission to a coherent user-visible outcome.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State Angular version, form structure and validation contract; verify form APIs in official documentation. Treat server errors as an added concrete context for explaining the source question.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains field and cross-field validation with clear ownership of error state.</li>
<li>Defines tests for valid input, invalid input and a rejected or overlapping submission.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equates client-side validation with enforcing the server&#x27;s business rules.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen if the user edits a field while its asynchronous validation is pending?</li>
<li>How would you display a server rejection without discarding the user&#x27;s input?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q006"></a>

### S06-Q006 · Failure cases

<p>How does a state change become an updated Angular view, and how would you diagnose a screen that renders slowly or fails to update?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q006](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q006)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q006](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q006)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain component rendering/change detection and common performance problems.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Change detection is the process connecting application changes to view updates. Explain the mechanism relevant to the actual application before selecting a performance fix.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Use a causal rendering model to distinguish correctness problems from expensive work.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify Angular version, change-detection/reactivity configuration and reproduction steps. Check official documentation rather than assuming current defaults or a particular runtime setup.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects an observable state transition to the expected view update.</li>
<li>Uses profiling or a minimal reproduction to distinguish competing causes and validate a repair.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Prescribes a named change-detection strategy without measuring the issue or checking the update path.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence distinguishes slow rendering from a slow network response?</li>
<li>How would you show that the fix keeps the view correct under repeated updates?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q007"></a>

### S06-Q007 · Trade-offs

<p>How would you organize state in a medium or large SPA so that screens can collaborate without losing clear ownership?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q007](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q007)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q007](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q007)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you structure state management for a medium or large SPA?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>State includes values a screen or the application must remember. Explain what needs to be shared, what remains local, and how changes stay understandable as features grow.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose state ownership and synchronization boundaries from concrete feature needs.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Describe the SPA&#x27;s collaboration requirements and selected Angular/state-library versions. Verify version-specific APIs in official documentation; no particular state library is required by the source.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Justifies local versus shared state using the lifetime and consumers of the data.</li>
<li>Explains how to test updates, stale responses and resets across navigation or identity changes.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Chooses a global store solely because the application is large, without identifying who owns each value.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which state should survive leaving a screen, and why?</li>
<li>How would you prevent two screens from maintaining conflicting copies of the same value?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q010"></a>

### S06-Q010 · Production decision

<p>How would you use bundle or code splitting to improve a frontend&#x27;s loading experience, and how would you verify the improvement?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q010](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q010)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q010](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q010)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain bundle/code splitting and frontend performance.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Code splitting separates application code into pieces that can be loaded at different times. Assess the whole loading experience, including later navigation, rather than only the first bundle&#x27;s size.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Make and validate a loading-performance decision from a real usage path.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify framework, build-tool versions, target device and network conditions. Consult official build documentation for relevant behavior; no performance result is supplied by the source.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects proposed boundaries to downloaded code and the work needed before a screen is usable.</li>
<li>Defines comparable before/after measurements and a later-navigation regression check.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claims success from a smaller initial bundle without measuring user-visible timing or additional requests.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would make splitting a frequently used feature counterproductive?</li>
<li>How would you distinguish download time from JavaScript execution cost?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Design an order editor reached through a lazily loaded route. Two editor panels need some shared values, validation can still be pending when the user submits, and users report a slow first visit. Draw responsibility and state-lifetime boundaries, trace one update, then propose separate checks for a failed load, an incorrect view update and slow rendering. Specify the Angular/build versions and verify applicable APIs before selecting a framework-specific repair.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Names the application parts and describes a working navigation and edit path.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends dependency and state boundaries, traces update and failure paths, and separates loading from rendering with a measurable validation plan.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A library or rendering strategy is prescribed without a reproduction, version context or observation that distinguishes the suspected cause.</p>
